create.name: Seattle Soto Zen
create.bio:
Seattle Soto Zen is a non-residential Zen community in Seattle, Washington, founded in 2010 and practising the forms of Soto Zen as handed down by Shunryu Suzuki and Dainin Katagiri. Eko Jeff Kelley guided the sangha through its first decade. Since 2019 its resident teacher has been Kanshin Allison Tait, a priest ordained by Zoketsu Norman Fischer who lived for around ten years at Tassajara and San Francisco Zen Center, trained as a Buddhist and interfaith chaplain, and received dharma transmission from Fischer in 2026.

The group has no temple of its own. On Sunday mornings it gathers in the Seattle Aikikai dojo on Capitol Hill for zazen, walking meditation, a dharma talk and a short chanting service, all shared on Zoom; on the first Sunday of each month the service becomes a well-being and memorial ceremony and newcomers can come early for an orientation. Online sitting runs every weekday morning, with brief beginners' instruction on Wednesdays, and the year adds practice-period classes, residential sesshin and one-day sits. Kanshin meets students for practice discussion in person or online, and recent talks are posted on the website.

courses.title: One-day Zazenkai – Rohatsu and the close of fall practice period
courses.description: A full day of sitting and walking meditation at Seattle Aikikai, with services, a dharma talk, small-group discussion and a bag lunch, closing the autumn practice period around the Buddha's enlightenment day. Online participants can follow the day on the usual Zoom link.
courses.price: Fee $30; Fee - Sustaining Level $60; Reduced Income $5; online free (donations welcome)

courses.title: Orientation for New Zen Practitioners
courses.description: A half-hour introduction before Sunday practice on the first Sunday of each month, covering how to sit, what happens in the zendo and any questions, for complete beginners or anyone wanting a refresher.

courses.title: Membership
courses.description: A regular pledge in any affordable amount that pays for practice space and the teacher's stipend and funds scholarships. Members get discounts on most programmes and can vote at annual meetings and stand for the board.
courses.price: $50/month: Basic supporting member; $100/month: Sustaining member; or an amount that suits your budget

free_resources.title: Recent Dharma Talks
free_resources.description: Video recordings of Sunday talks, mostly by Kanshin Allison Tait with others by lay teachers and senior students, on zazen, Dogen, koans and the practice period texts.

free_resources.title: Practice with Us Online
free_resources.description: Open Zoom sittings every weekday morning, early sittings three days a week, Wednesday beginners' instruction and the Sunday programme, with the chant book and class materials linked.
